summary: José Carlos Ribeiro Calazans Duarte is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed degrees across multiple institutions, including a doctorate at Lusófona University (2006–2012), where he served as an assistant professor from 2006 to 2021.

José Ignacio Cabezón works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Caltech, Sera Monastery, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, he held posts at Iliff School of Theology and UCSB, where he became Dalai Lama Professor in 2001.

José Ventura Traveset (1862–1941) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under Francisco García Ayuso. He served as Professor of Humanities at the University of Granada (1887–1889) and as a professor at the University of Valencia from 1901.
Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2012).

Jowita Kramer is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and habilitated at Munich; she taught at Munich (2017–2021) and became a professor at the University of Leipzig in 2021.
Joy Brennan works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, and Constance Furey.

Joyce Burkhalter Flueckiger is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She studied at Goshen College and the University of Wisconsin-Madison before serving on the faculty at Emory University (~1992–2022), where she is Professor Emerita.

Joydeb Dinda is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who completed a PhD at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute by 2022. In 2022, he became an assistant professor at Laxmi Devi Shroff Adarsh Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya.

Jozef Deleu (1925–1994) was an Indology scholar who earned his BA and doctorate at Ghent University under Adriaan Scharpé and studied at Hamburg. After teaching in secondary schools, he served as docent in Indology at Ghent University (1964–1990).

João Carlos Barbosa Gonçalves is an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who earned a PhD in linguistics from the University of São Paulo (2005–2009). He served as a professor at the State University of Campinas (2003–2005) and USP (2014–2015).

Juan Gelabert y Gordiola (1843–1894) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Francisco García Ayuso, completed his PhD at Complutense University of Madrid by 1868, and served there as Professor of Sanskrit from 1883 to 1894.
Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Cardiff University under the supervision of Max Deeg (attested 2012).

Judit Törzsök is an Indologist who earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. She taught at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III and Lille before becoming a directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2018.

Judith Simmer-Brown is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who earned a PhD from Walden University. Since 1977, she has served at Naropa University, where she became Distinguished Professor of Contemplative and Religious Studies Emerita.

Judith Snodgrass is a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her BA and PhD from the University of Sydney and served as an associate professor at Western Sydney University from 1991 to 2016.

Juhn Y. Ahn is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 2007. He holds a faculty appointment at the University of Michigan, serving as Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies (attested 2019).

Juhyung Rhi specializes in Buddhist studies, art history, and Indology. After earning a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, he became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University in 1992.
Juichiro Tanabe is a scholar in philosophy who studied as a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford (2000–2001) and trained under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire (1805–1895) was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He served as professor of Greek and Latin philosophy at the Collège de France (1838–1852) and belonged to the Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques.

Jules Bloch (1880–1953) was a French Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet. His career included posts at EPHE, INALCO, the University of Paris, and the Collège de France, where he held the Sanskrit chair (1936–1951).
